Dear ^pal_fname^,

I am writing to ask for your help with an important survey about what ^pal_intro1^ doing now that ^pal_intro2^ have ^pal_intro3^ school. The survey only takes around ^pal_mins^ minutes to complete and will provide important information to help plan future school programs in the ACT. The survey includes questions about satisfaction with school, current study, and employment.

Please complete the survey by clicking on the button below:

Start Survey

Complete the survey now to go into a prize draw for a $1,000 prepaid VISA gift card.*

The Social Research Centre is conducting this survey on behalf of the ACT Education Directorate. Both organisations will handle all personal information in accordance with the ACT Privacy Principles set out in the Information Privacy Act 2014. The survey results will be used in public interest research projects and longitudinal studies aimed at improving the quality of services in the ACT. All your answers are private and confidential. No individuals will be identified, and no personal information will be provided to any school or college.

If you have any questions or would like to be excluded from the survey, please call the Social Research Centre (freecall) on 1800 023 040, email actyr12@srcentre.com.au, or visit srcentre.com.au/project/actsurveyinfo.

Although the survey is voluntary, I hope you will want to participate. We are working hard to empower Canberra’s young people to learn for life and your feedback will help inform our decisions. Previous survey publications can be found on the Education Directorate’s web site, education.act.gov.au.


Yours sincerely,

Michael Crowther
Executive Branch Manager
Analytics and Evaluation Branch

*Complete the survey online by 09/06/2024 to go into the prize draw to win a $1,000 prepaid VISA gift card 

Trouble accessing the survey? Try copying and pasting the URL below into your browser.

We’d like to understand more about your experiences and settlement needs

Dear ^f('first_name')^

Thank you for participating in our first survey of recent migrants, which you responded to in 2024.

As mentioned during the first survey, we would like your assistance again to complete a follow-up questionnaire about your settlement experiences over the last 12 months. Your participation in this follow-up survey will play a vital role in helping the Department of Home Affairs improve its policies and programs for current and future migrants to Australia.

The Social Research Centre will try and make contact with you from September to complete this survey over the phone, alternatively, you can complete it on a smartphone, tablet or PC by clicking on the button below:

Start Survey

If you are having any trouble accessing the survey, please go to www.srcentre.com.au/srma and click on the “Start Survey” button. Your Login Code is: ^f('UserId')^

If you do not complete the survey online, you will be contacted by telephone. The telephone survey will take 15 to 20 minutes, depending on your answers. Calls to complete the follow-up survey will come from one of the phone numbers listed on our website at www.srcentre.com.au/srma. If you receive a missed call from one of these numbers, it is in relation to the survey.

To update your current telephone number, or if you have any other questions about the survey, please call the Social Research Centre on 1800 830 220 or email csam@srcentre.com.au (mention reference number: 3373srma). We will only keep your contact details for the final survey

The survey includes questions about your partner (detailed in the box below). Please make this information available to your partner before you commence the survey.

For further information about the survey see www.homeaffairs.gov.au/srma and for an overview of some findings from the first survey, see CSAM Results Summary (274 KB, PDF).

 

Please share the following information with your partner before commencing this survey.

The survey primarily focusses on collecting information about recent migrants (including new visa holders) to understand their experiences in migrating to Australia.

The survey also collects information on partners of recent migrants and/or new visa holders to understand experiences for this group of individuals. To do this, the survey will ask for some information about you. This can include personal information, such as employment status and income. Please note, all information collected will be de-identified and maintained in the strictest of confidence.

If you do not want this information to be collected in the survey, please let your partner know so they can skip these questions about you.

 

Thank you for taking part in this important survey.

Yours sincerely

Eugen Kovac

Manager, Continuous Survey of Australia’s Migrants

Data and Economic Analysis Centre

Department of Home Affairs

 

Authorised by:

Department of Home Affairs

Note.Name: README
Note.Text:
## Overview

This repository contains the Forsta integration for Research Defender (RD). It
wraps both the client-side scripts that call the RD APIs and the server-side
logic that verifies responses and determines whether a respondent can continue
through the survey.

At a high level the integration:

- Collects RD Search V4 and RD Activity data into two Forsta text-list
  questions, `RD_Search` and `RD_Activity`.
- Validates and hashes RD Search data on the server before trusting the client
  payload.
- Retrieves RD Activity statistics server-side using an API token obtained in
  the browser.
- Aggregates the outcomes into a single-value question
  `research_defender_fail` where `0 = allow respondent to continue`,
  `1 = terminate respondent`.

## Configuration

The implementation is configured in the `consts` script. There are two steps
for configuration the project:

1. Fill in the `projectSettings` object (see comments for instructions)
2. Uncomment one of the template configs depending on the type of project.
   It is vital that this is set selected correctly because all of the termination
   logic depens on the values of this config. The defaults align with the company
   standard settings: 
   https://srcentre.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/AuditRiskandPrivacyCommittee/IQCcJahzDWdjRKFloXNC2qfeASJqFJQ_sPub2XwMWw4XtuQ?e=sUGs8X


## Data flow

1. Landing page (`client/onlineIntro.js`) unhides the intro content and the 
   next button only when RD calls finish. It listens for custom events fired by
   the producer scripts so the respondent cannot continue until responses are
   available.
2. **RD Search (`client/search.js`)** runs client-side, calls the RD Search V4
   endpoint, stores the raw payload and HTTP status into `RD_Search`, then fires
   the completion event.
3. **RD Activity token fetch (`client/activity.js`)** runs client-side, calls the
   RD Activity token endpoint, stores the raw token payload and HTTP status into
   `RD_Activity`, then fires its completion event.
4. **Server script (`rd.js`)** executes after the page submits. It parses and
   validates `RD_Search` via `processSearchResults()`, pulls statistics for
   `RD_Activity` via `processActivityResults()`, and finally computes
   `research_defender_fail` inside `determineOverallPassFail()`.

## Client-side behaviour

### search.js

- Uses `fetch` with credentials and an 8-second timeout supplied by Forsta macros
  (`^getTimeout()^`, `^makeRDSearchURL()^`).
- Writes `status_code` and `raw_response` to `RD_Search`.
- Emits a custom event (`^getSearchEventName()^`) so the intro screen can
  re-enable navigation.

### activity.js

- Calls the RD Activity token endpoint with the public API key. Response text
  goes into `RD_Activity.raw_token_response`, HTTP status into `status_code`.
- Emits a second custom event (`^getActivityEventName()^`) and unhides the intro
  once both events are received.

### onlineIntro.js

- Waits for both events (or detects prefilled hidden inputs) before restoring
  the original intro content and un-hiding buttons, preventing users from
  skipping the RD checks.

## Security considerations

The RD Search V4 endpoint supports signing the request URL with the private key
so Research Defender can confirm it was not tampered with. RD also signs the
response payload: `Validation.Surveys` and `Validation.Respondent` are hashes of
the corresponding entries in the `String` object. Because those string values are
not valid JSON, we extract key-value pairs via regular expressions to ensure the
data we trust matches what was signed. We should pursue a native, structured
response with RD to avoid depending on this workaround.

## HTTP status codes and timeouts

Both client scripts use an 8-second timeout. If a request does not complete in
time, it is aborted; the server interprets this as a failure since allowing the
respondent through would let malicious users block outbound traffic to bypass
screening. Every response captures the HTTP status code so we can differentiate
between network issues and valid RD denials.
